correctness.rationale: Uniform Cayley trees are counted by Matrix–Tree. A two-marked-vertex cofactor with nested allowed neighbor sets A,B (and forbidden marked edge) has F_n(a,b)=ab n^(b-1)(n-1)^(a-b)(n-2)^(n-a-3). Schur complement and rank-two determinant lemma establish this identity, with one-vertex isolation p_(n,h)=(n-h)/n*(1-1/n)^(h-2). For a time pair j<=k, partition ordered marked vertex choices into identical vertices (j), two already revealed vertices (j(j-1)), and earlier+newly revealed vertices (j(k-j)), yielding exact cross moment j p_k+j(j-1)u+j(k-j)v. Subtract jk p_j p_k. First-order expansion of the two joint-to-product ratios yields the stated strictly positive rank-two semiseparable kernel K(s,t)=s(1-t)e^-t[1-(1-s)e^-s+s(2-s)(1-t)e^-s] for 0<s<=t<1. Boundary conditions j>=2,k<n; no claim of Gaussian process convergence. Independent Prüfer enumeration checked all (j,k) cases for n=4,5,6.

The audited new part is the nested unequal-neighbor Matrix–Tree count and two-time isolate covariance. Resultary related Cayley tree degree-distance and recursive leaf covariance records are different observables. A general multitime forest formula could cover it; retain that risk.
